01-contract-first-api-scaffolder.name: Contract-First API Scaffolder
01-contract-first-api-scaffolder.trigger: User provides an OpenAPI spec, GraphQL schema, or a plain-language description of an API endpoint/resource. User says things like "scaffold this endpoint", "generate the API for…
01-contract-first-api-scaffolder.summary: Generates backend route handlers + validation models AND the matching frontend client types/hooks in a single pass, so the two never drift out of sync.

02-dependency-graph-impact-analyzer.name: Dependency-Graph Impact Analyzer
02-dependency-graph-impact-analyzer.trigger: Before any non-trivial refactor, rename, or signature change. User says "what will this break", "what depends on this", "impact of changing X".
02-dependency-graph-impact-analyzer.summary: Statically traces every module, route, test, and caller that touches the function/class being changed, and produces a blast-radius report before any edit is made.

03-migration-safe-schema-editor.name: Migration-Safe Schema Editor
03-migration-safe-schema-editor.trigger: Any change to an ORM model, SQL table definition, or database schema. User says "add a column", "change this model", "update the schema".
03-migration-safe-schema-editor.summary: Diffs the proposed model change against the current schema and generates the matching migration file (Alembic/Prisma/Django/etc., detect from repo) plus a working rollback.

04-test-gap-finder.name: Test Gap Finder
04-test-gap-finder.trigger: User says "find missing tests", "improve coverage", "what's untested here". After adding new logic with conditional branches.
04-test-gap-finder.summary: Runs (or reads) coverage data and generates tests specifically for uncovered branches — not a blanket regeneration of the whole test suite.

05-prompt-response-regression-harness.name: Prompt/Response Regression Harness
05-prompt-response-regression-harness.trigger: Any change to a prompt template, model version, or NLP/ML pipeline step. User says "did this prompt change break anything", "compare model outputs".
05-prompt-response-regression-harness.summary: Snapshots prompts and their outputs, then flags when the same input starts producing a meaningfully different output after a change.

06-env-secrets-drift-checker.name: Env/Secrets Drift Checker
06-env-secrets-drift-checker.trigger: Before a deploy. User says "check my env vars", "why is this failing in prod", "deploy readiness check".
06-env-secrets-drift-checker.summary: Diffs `.env.example` (or equivalent) against what the code actually reads (`os.getenv`, `process.env`, config classes) and against deployment platform env vars if accessible, flagging missing or unused keys before runtime failure.

07-doc-sync.name: Doc-Sync Skill
07-doc-sync.trigger: Any change to a function/method signature, public API, or exported type. User says "update the docs", "keep docs in sync".
07-doc-sync.summary: Detects signature/behavior changes and updates the corresponding README section, docstring, and API reference in the same change, so docs don't silently rot.

08-xml-document-structure-validator.name: XML/Document-Structure Validator
08-xml-document-structure-validator.trigger: Working with XML, DOCX-internal XML, XSD-bound documents, or any schema-validated document format. User says "validate this XML", "why is this document invalid", "check against …
08-xml-document-structure-validator.summary: Validates a document against its schema (XSD/DTD/RelaxNG) and translates raw parser errors into plain-language explanations with a suggested fix.

09-cross-repo-context-linker.name: Cross-Repo Context Linker
09-cross-repo-context-linker.trigger: Multi-service or multi-repo projects where a change in one repo affects another (e.g., a shared architecture like IRIS with separate modules). User says "check how this is used …
09-cross-repo-context-linker.summary: Pulls relevant context (interfaces, shared types, config contracts) from sibling repos/modules without the user manually pasting files in.

10-performance-regression-sentinel.name: Performance Regression Sentinel
10-performance-regression-sentinel.trigger: Changes to hot paths: inference calls, tight loops, DB queries, anything previously identified as performance-sensitive. User says "check for perf regressions", "benchmark this …
10-performance-regression-sentinel.summary: Benchmarks the affected code path before and after a change and flags if latency/memory crosses a set threshold — especially useful around ML/NLP inference calls.

11-design-token-enforcer.name: Design-Token Enforcer
11-design-token-enforcer.trigger: Any new or modified UI component. User says "check this against our design tokens", "fix hardcoded styles".
11-design-token-enforcer.summary: Scans components for hardcoded colors, spacing, and font values and rewrites them against the project's existing design tokens/theme variables.

12-motion-interaction-reviewer.name: Motion/Interaction Reviewer
12-motion-interaction-reviewer.trigger: New or changed interactive component (buttons, cards, modals, nav items). User says "review the interactions", "check states/animations".
12-motion-interaction-reviewer.summary: Flags missing hover/focus/active/disabled states and inconsistent transition timing, and proposes a concrete motion spec instead of just noting what's missing.

13-accessibility-auditor.name: Accessibility Auditor (with fix-patches)
13-accessibility-auditor.trigger: Any UI component work. User says "check accessibility", "a11y audit", "is this compliant".
13-accessibility-auditor.summary: Runs axe-core-style checks conceptually against the rendered/markup output and generates an actual patch (aria labels, contrast fixes, focus order) instead of just a report.

14-component-api-critic.name: Component API Critic
14-component-api-critic.trigger: New component being added to a shared component library. User says "review this component's props/API", "is this consistent with our other components".
14-component-api-critic.summary: Reviews new component props against the conventions already established elsewhere in the library (naming, boolean vs.

15-visual-regression-diffing-agent.name: Visual Regression Diffing Agent
15-visual-regression-diffing-agent.trigger: Any change to component styling or layout. User says "check for visual regressions", "did this change break the layout".
15-visual-regression-diffing-agent.summary: Compares before/after rendered output of a component at multiple breakpoints and highlights actual pixel-level/layout differences, not just "the code changed."

16-empty-state-generator.name: Empty-State / Edge-State Generator
16-empty-state-generator.trigger: Any list, table, dashboard, or data-driven component. User says "handle the empty state", "what about loading/errors".
16-empty-state-generator.summary: Auto-generates the loading, empty, error, and overflow states for a data-driven component — the states usually forgotten until QA finds them.

17-latency-aware-skeleton-builder.name: Latency-Aware UI Skeleton Builder
17-latency-aware-skeleton-builder.trigger: Building a loading state for a component backed by a real API call. User says "add a loading state", "this loading feels off".

18-design-to-code-diff-checker.name: Design-to-Code Diff Checker
18-design-to-code-diff-checker.trigger: A Figma frame/link or design spec is provided alongside implemented code. User says "does this match the design", "check against Figma".
18-design-to-code-diff-checker.summary: Compares the shipped component against the provided design reference (spacing, type scale, colors, si

19-multi-theme-consistency-checker.name: Multi-Theme Consistency Checker
19-multi-theme-consistency-checker.trigger: App supports dark/light/brand or other theme variants. User says "check this in dark mode", "does this work across themes".
19-multi-theme-consistency-checker.summary: Verifies a new or changed component renders correctly across every supported theme variant, not just the one it was built/tested in.

20-narrative-state-debugger.name: Narrative-State Debugger for Agentic UIs
20-narrative-state-debugger.trigger: Multi-step AI/agent-driven interfaces (assistant UIs, conversational agents, multi-turn workflows like a JARVIS-style system or an analysis pipeline with a UI). User says "the U…
20-narrative-state-debugger.summary: Traces a session's UI state transitions against the underlying agent/session state and flags where they've desynced — a common bug class in AI-driven interfaces where the UI shows a stale step, wrong status, or mismatched output.

21-code-complexity-reducer.name: Code Complexity Reducer
21-code-complexity-reducer.trigger: User says "simplify this", "reduce complexity", "this function is too complex". Any function with deep nesting, long parameter lists, or high branching.
21-code-complexity-reducer.summary: Scans for cyclomatic complexity, deep nesting, and long parameter lists, then proposes concrete refactors ranked by complexity-reduction-per-line-changed — not style nitpicks.

22-apple-hig-design.name: Apple HIG Design Skill
22-apple-hig-design.trigger: Building or reviewing UI intended for iOS/macOS or targeting an "Apple-native" feel. User says "make this feel native", "Apple-style design", "check against HIG".
22-apple-hig-design.summary: Applies Apple's Human Interface Guidelines: correct spacing/type scale, native navigation and gesture patterns, proper use of materials/blur/depth, and platform-appropriate controls — flags anything that reads as non-native.

23-fast-task-completion-mode.name: Fast Task Completion Mode
23-fast-task-completion-mode.trigger: User explicitly requests speed: "just do it", "fast mode", "don't overthink this", or the task is clearly well-scoped and low-ambiguity.
23-fast-task-completion-mode.summary: A lean execution mode for well-scoped tasks: skips exploratory discussion, batches reads/edits instead of doing them one at a time, defaults to the most conventional implementation without presenting multiple options, and only pauses for ge

24-secrets-credential-leak-scanner.name: Secrets/Credential Leak Scanner
24-secrets-credential-leak-scanner.trigger: Before any git push/commit. User says "check for leaked secrets", "scan for exposed keys".
24-secrets-credential-leak-scanner.summary: Scans working diffs AND git history (not just `.env` files) for hardcoded API keys, tokens, and credentials, matching known key-format patterns (AWS, Stripe, OpenAI, GitHub, JWTs, etc.) before a push.

25-i18n-localization-completeness-checke.name: i18n/Localization Completeness Checker
25-i18n-localization-completeness-checke.trigger: Adding or changing user-facing text in an app with translation files. User says "check translations", "i18n audit".
25-i18n-localization-completeness-checke.summary: Diffs translation files against the base locale, flags missing keys, unused keys, and raw user-facing strings that were never wrapped in the translation function.

26-dead-code-unused-export-finder.name: Dead Code & Unused Export Finder
26-dead-code-unused-export-finder.trigger: User says "find dead code", "clean up unused exports", periodic codebase hygiene pass.
26-dead-code-unused-export-finder.summary: Traces the full import graph across the codebase to find exported functions/components/routes that nothing references anymore — a whole-codebase audit, distinct from pre-change impact analysis.

27-bundle-size-auditor.name: Bundle Size Auditor
27-bundle-size-auditor.trigger: Adding a new dependency, or user says "check bundle si
27-bundle-size-auditor.summary: Flags what a new dependency/import actually costs in bundle si

28-flaky-test-detector.name: Flaky Test Detector
28-flaky-test-detector.trigger: A test fails intermittently, or user says "this test is flaky", "why does this fail randomly".
28-flaky-test-detector.summary: Reruns the suite/test multiple times to isolate intermittent failures, then diagnoses the likely cause instead of just labeling it "flaky" and moving on.

29-feature-flag-lifecycle-manager.name: Feature Flag Lifecycle Manager
29-feature-flag-lifecycle-manager.trigger: Adding a new feature flag, or user says "audit feature flags", "clean up flags".
29-feature-flag-lifecycle-manager.summary: Tracks flags from creation to cleanup: flags ones at 100% rollout for a while that should be deleted, and warns when new code adds a permanent dependency on a supposedly-temporary flag.

30-changelog-release-notes-generator.name: Changelog/Release Notes Generator
30-changelog-release-notes-generator.trigger: Preparing a release/tag, or user says "generate changelog", "draft release notes".
30-changelog-release-notes-generator.summary: Reads merged commits/PRs since the last tag and drafts categori

31-api-rate-limit-backoff-auditor.name: API Rate-Limit & Backoff Auditor
31-api-rate-limit-backoff-auditor.trigger: Adding a call to an external API, or user says "check retry logic", "will this hit rate limits".
31-api-rate-limit-backoff-auditor.summary: Checks external API calls for missing retry/backoff logic, flags calls with no rate-limit handling, and generates an exponential-backoff wrapper matching the target API's documented limits.

32-config-parity-checker.name: Config Parity Across Environments Checker
32-config-parity-checker.trigger: User says "check config drift", "compare staging and prod config", before a deploy.
32-config-parity-checker.summary: Compares dev/staging/prod config (feature flags, timeouts, limits, resource si

33-error-logging-consistency-enforcer.name: Error/Logging Consistency Enforcer
33-error-logging-consistency-enforcer.trigger: Adding error handling/logging, or user says "check logging consistency", "standardi
33-error-logging-consistency-enforcer.summary: Checks that errors are logged with a consistent structure (level, context fields, stack trace inclusion) across the codebase, instead of every file inventing its own shape.

34-commit-message-quality-skill.name: Commit Message Quality Skill
34-commit-message-quality-skill.trigger: Ready to commit staged changes, or user says "write a commit message", "draft a commit".
34-commit-message-quality-skill.summary: Reviews staged changes and drafts a commit message matching the repo's actual convention (conventional commits, ticket-prefix style, imperative one-liners, etc.), inferred from git log history — not a generic template.

35-full-app-from-prompt-builder.name: Full-App-From-Prompt Builder
35-full-app-from-prompt-builder.trigger: User gives a plain product description and wants a working app, not just a single file/component. User says "build me an app that...", "scaffold a full product for...".
35-full-app-from-prompt-builder.summary: Takes a plain-language product description and scaffolds a complete, architecturally coherent app in one pass — frontend, backend, data model, auth — with a written rationale for each structural decision, not a pile of disconnected files.

36-self-healing-build-loop.name: Self-Healing Build Loop
36-self-healing-build-loop.trigger: After generating or modifying code, before presenting it as finished. User says "make sure this actually builds/passes", "fix it until it works".
36-self-healing-build-loop.summary: After every generated change, runs build/lint/test, parses the actual error output, and iterates fixes autonomously up to a capped attempt count — then reports plainly what it couldn't resolve, instead of claiming success it didn't verify.

37-multi-agent-task-orchestrator.name: Multi-Agent Task Orchestrator
37-multi-agent-task-orchestrator.trigger: A task is large enough that one flat pass tends to lose coherence (a full feature, a multi-file refactor, a full app). User says "break this down and handle it properly", "this …
37-multi-agent-task-orchestrator.summary: Breaks a large task into explicit roles — planner, implementer, reviewer, tester — with defined handoff contracts between them, so a big task doesn't collapse under one undifferentiated context pass.

38-autonomous-root-cause-debugger.name: Autonomous Root-Cause Debugger
38-autonomous-root-cause-debugger.trigger: Given a bug report, error message, or stack trace. User says "why is this happening", "debug this", "find the root cause".
38-autonomous-root-cause-debugger.summary: Forms hypotheses, adds targeted instrumentation, reproduces the failure, and narrows to root cause before writing any fix — no shotgun patching based on a guess.

39-live-architecture-decision-recorder.name: Live Architecture Decision Recorder
39-live-architecture-decision-recorder.trigger: A significant technical fork during a build: choosing a library, a data model shape, an auth strategy, a pattern for state management. User says "log this decision", "write an A…
39-live-architecture-decision-recorder.summary: Automatically writes a lightweight ADR (what was decided, why, alternatives considered) at each significant technical fork, so decisions and their reasoning aren't lost by the next session.

40-spec-to-build-plan-converter.name: Spec-to-Build-Plan Converter
40-spec-to-build-plan-converter.trigger: User has a loose product idea and wants it built, but hasn't specified a structured plan. User says "here's my idea, build it" or similar unstructured product asks.
40-spec-to-build-plan-converter.summary: Converts a loose product idea into a structured plan — data model, user flows, milestone sequence — before any code gets written, front-loading planning the way high-end app-builder tools do.

41-multimodal-spec-binder.name: Multimodal Spec Binder
41-multimodal-spec-binder.trigger: A screenshot, error capture, or design mockup is pasted into the conversation mid-task. User says "here's what it looks like", "here's the error", "match this design".
41-multimodal-spec-binder.summary: Treats pasted images as first-class spec input, cross-referenced directly against the actual code — not as loose context that gets mentioned once and then ignored.

42-continuous-quality-gate.name: Continuous Quality Gate
42-continuous-quality-gate.trigger: Before declaring any task "done" or "complete". User says "is this actually ready", "final check before I ship this".
42-continuous-quality-gate.summary: Runs a fixed checklist before calling anything complete — tests, lint, types, no console warnings/errors, basic accessibility pass — and reports gate status explicitly rather than declaring completion on vibes.

43-autonomous-adversarial-reviewer.name: Autonomous Adversarial Reviewer
43-autonomous-adversarial-reviewer.trigger: After generating a diff, before presenting it as final. User says "review this like a senior engineer would", "be harsh about this".
43-autonomous-adversarial-reviewer.summary: Reviews its own generated diff the way a strict senior engineer would before presenting it — catching the issues a first pass reliably misses, rather than presenting first-draft output as final.

44-prototype-to-production-hardener.name: Prototype-to-Production Hardener
44-prototype-to-production-hardener.trigger: Taking a fast throwaway prototype toward something real. User says "harden this for production", "this was just a quick prototype, make it real".
44-prototype-to-production-hardener.summary: Systematically upgrades a prototype — error handling, input validation, security basics, env/config management — and lists exactly what was hardened and what's still a known shortcut.

45-caveman-compressed-mode.name: Caveman Compressed Mode
45-caveman-compressed-mode.trigger: User explicitly requests compressed/low-token output: "caveman mode", "compress this", "cut the filler", "be terse", "minimi
45-caveman-compressed-mode.summary: Rewrites the agent's own output into stripped-down, filler-free technical prose — dropping hedges, pleasantries, restated context, and throat-clearing — while preserving exact technical accuracy.
